'''Murray Seymour Klamkin''' (March 5, 1921 – August 6, 2004) was an American [[mathematician]], known as prolific proposer and editor of professionally-challenging mathematical problems.

==Life==
Klamkin was born on March 5, 1921, in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York City|New York]]. He received a bachelor's degree from the [[Cooper Union]] in 1942 and, after four years of service in the United States Army, earned a master's degree from the [[Polytechnic University of New York|Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]] in 1947, where he taught from 1948 until 1957.

After this, Klamkin worked at [[AVCO]], taught at [[University at Buffalo, The State University of New York|SUNY Buffalo]] (1962&ndash;1964), and served as the principal research scientist at [[Ford Motor Company]] (1965&ndash;1976).  During this period, he was also a visiting professor at the [[University of Minnesota]].  After leaving Ford, he became a professor at the [[University of Waterloo]].<ref>[http://www.maa.org/mathhorizons/volume/klamkin.htm ''Memorial Celebration of the Life of Murray Seymour Klamkin''], web page at the MAA, accessed 2007-01-11.</ref> 
From 1976 to 1981 Klamkin was the chairman of the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Alberta]].<ref>[https://www.ualberta.ca/ARCHIVES/guide/3FACULTY/92.htm ''University of Alberta Archives: Faculty of Science''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130615013606/https://www.ualberta.ca/ARCHIVES/guide/3FACULTY/92.htm |date=2013-06-15 }}, web page at the University of Alberta, accessed 2007-01-11.</ref>

After 1981 he became an [[emeritus]] professor at Alberta.  Klamkin died August 6, 2004.<ref>[http://www.maa.org/sites/default/files/pdf/pubs/nov04.pdf ''Murray Klamkin, 1921-2004''], ''MAA FOCUS''  '''24''' (#8), November 2004, p. 32, accessed 2014-03-03.</ref>

==Mathematical problems==
Klamkin was known worldwide as a prolific proposer and editor of professionally challenging mathematical problems.  He served as problem editor for ''[[SIAM Review]]'', the ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]'', ''[[Math Horizons]]'', and other journals.  He was also known for his work in high-level [[mathematics competitions]], such as the [[United States of America Mathematical Olympiad|USA Mathematical Olympiad]], the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], and the [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition|Putnam Competition]].  
In 1988 the [[Mathematical Association of America]] gave him its Award for Distinguished Service to Mathematics, its highest service award.<ref>"Award for Distinguished Service to Prof. Murray Klamkin", [[Gerald L. Alexanderson]], ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]'' '''95''' (#1), January 1988, pp. 1&ndash;4.</ref>  In 1992, the [[World Federation of National Mathematics Competitions]] awarded Klamkin  the [[David Hilbert Award]] for his contributions to mathematics competitions.<ref>[http://www.amt.edu.au/wfnmcaw.html ''David Hilbert and Paul Erdös Awards''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171231160201/http://www.amt.edu.au/wfnmcaw.html |date=2017-12-31 }}, web page at the WFNMC, accessed 2014-03-03.</ref>

==Selected bibliography==
* "The asymmetric propeller", [[Leon Bankoff]], Paul Erdös, and Murray S. Klamkin, ''Mathematics Magazine'' '''46''', #5 (November 1973), pp.&nbsp;270&ndash;272.
* ''International Mathematical Olympiads, 1978&ndash;1985 and Forty Supplementary Problems'', ed. Murray S. Klamkin, pub. Washington, DC: [[Mathematical Association of America]], 1986.  {{ISBN|0-88385-631-X}}.
* ''Mathematical Modelling: Classroom Notes in Applied Mathematics'', ed. Murray S. Klamkin, pub. Philadelphia, PA: [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], 1987.  {{ISBN|0-89871-204-1}}.
* ''U.S.A. Mathematical Olympiads, 1972&ndash;1986'', ed. Murray S. Klamkin, pub. Washington, DC: Mathematical Association of America, 1988.  {{ISBN|0-88385-634-4}}.
* ''Problems in Applied Mathematics: Selections from SIAM Review'', ed. Murray S. Klamkin, pub. Philadelphia, PA: Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics, 1990.  {{ISBN|0-89871-259-9}}.
* ''Five Hundred Mathematical Challenges'', Edward J. Barbeau, Murray S. Klamkin, and William O. J. Moser, pub. Washington, DC: Mathematical Association of America, 1995.  {{ISBN|0-88385-519-4}}.
* {{cite book | editor1-last = Liu | editor1-first = Andy | editor2-last = Shawyer | editor2-first = Bruce | title = Problems from Murray Klamkin | publisher = Mathematical Association of America | location = Washington | year = 2008 | isbn = 978-0-88385-828-8 }} A collection of problems posed by Klamkin in ''[[Crux Mathematicorum with Mathematical Mayhem]]''.
